scope: Confirm distributed cancellation before reporting completed revocation
invariant: A completed revocation requires authenticated confirmation that every obligated authority stopped the affected actions and control.
existing_semantics: The current issuer reply confirms a durable revocation commit. It does not claim distributed cancellation completion.
baseline_result: A remote actor moved after the issuer commit reply while a relay held the real event. Motion stopped after delivery.
required_evidence: Authenticate each world and workspace authority as its own service participant, distinct from actor identity.
Bind participant registration and acknowledgements to the issuer, domain, process incarnation, and current connection.
Include all admitted execution and presentation authorities in the revocation obligations.
Deny new affected work immediately after authoritative revocation. Drain existing affected work before acknowledging completion.
Acknowledge only after native input release, motion cancellation, observation withdrawal, lease release, and required process termination are confirmed.
Credential revocation does not terminate applications with independently valid execution authority.
Parent and actor revocation invalidate dependent grants while independent grants remain usable.
A lost connection, expired wait, crashed authority, or issuer restart cannot count as successful cancellation.
Preserve pending obligations and durable revocation across crashes. Reconcile explicitly without replaying uncertain actions.
Reject stale, forged, duplicate-conflicting, wrong-domain, and wrong-incarnation acknowledgements.
New participants synchronize current authority before accepting actions; they cannot escape a concurrent revocation.
Run delayed delivery, blocked native cancellation, in-flight operation, and multi-host witnesses through production components.
Qualify complete Debug and runtime sanitizer profiles on both allowed hosts. Preserve locked acceptance tests.
implementation_constraints: Record additive protobuf interfaces and explicit persistence migration before implementation.
Keep issuer commit status distinct from distributed cancellation completion.
A background watcher receiving an event is not a cancellation acknowledgement.
Use a contiguous applied revision, not the maximum observed feed head.
Do not treat removal from a socket list as proof that an authority stopped.
Do not replace missing evidence with sleeps, per-request credential checks, or a successful local database transaction.
No model inference or additional host is needed for this component.
Do not modify the active remote-transport candidate.
next_test: An owner observes committed-but-pending revocation while one enrolled authority delays cancellation, then observes completion only after genuine cancellation acknowledgement.
limitations: The diagnostic reproduces a known missing requirement. It is not passing M02 acceptance.
Participant registration, barrier persistence, and acknowledgement interfaces are not implemented yet.
Native input and multi-host cancellation barrier evidence remains unrun.
